core_obligations: Reduce to the Noetherian case (proof lines 13063-13072): by absolute Noetherian approximation write X = lim X_t with each X_t of finite type over Spec(Z) and affine transition morphisms; the colimit description of constructible sheaves makes F the pullback of a constructible F_t over some X_t.

Apply the Noetherian case (proof lines 13073-13080): the Noetherian statement gives an injection of F_t into a finite product of f_{i,*}underline{E_i} (in the set case) or a finite direct sum of f_{i,*}underline{M_i} (in the abelian and Lambda-module cases), with f_i : Y_i -> X_t finite, the morphisms being of finite presentation because X_t is Noetherian.

Pull back along X -> X_t (proof lines 13081-13088): pullback is exact and formation of the finite pushforwards commutes with base change, so pulling the embedding back gives the asserted injective map over X, in each of the three cases.
proof_roadmap: Write X as a limit of Noetherian approximants and descend the constructible sheaf to one stage.
Apply the Noetherian form of the embedding theorem at that stage, noting the finite morphisms are of finite presentation.
Pull the embedding back to X using exactness of pullback and base change for finite pushforwards.
difficulty_reason: The lemma generalises the embedding of a constructible sheaf into a finite product or sum of pushforwards of constant sheaves from Noetherian schemes to quasi-compact quasi-separated ones (statement lines 13027-13060). The proof (proof lines 13062-13088) is a descent through absolute Noetherian approximation: the constructible sheaf appears over some approximant by the colimit description, the Noetherian case supplies the embedding there, and pullback together with base change for finite pushforwards transports it back to X. H2: one approximation-and-descent argument, written out. The statement carries the author's reference to SGA4 IX 2.14, retained verbatim.
